# kaf-mirror

> kaf-mirror is Kafka backup you can watch, audit and trust. It is one server binary with a dashboard. It makes exact copies, in partition order, with idempotent writes, and resumes from the last committed offset after a restart. It has RBAC, an audit trail, compliance reports, and Replication halt (tech preview). Apache Kafka, Confluent, Redpanda and Azure Event Hubs can be the source or the target, and KafScale is a supported target for a backup on S3. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and written in Go.

The latest release is [v2.0.0](https://github.com/scalytics/kaf-mirror/releases/tag/v2.0.0), published 27 November 2026. Read the [upgrade notes](https://github.com/scalytics/kaf-mirror/blob/main/RELEASE_v2.0.0.md) and the Breaking section of the [changelog](https://github.com/scalytics/kaf-mirror/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) before you upgrade. The image `ghcr.io/scalytics/kaf-mirror:v2.0.0` is published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The server and `admin-cli` binaries are Linux amd64 only. `mirror-cli` is also available for Linux arm64, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows amd64.

What it does:

- A job consumes from a source cluster and produces to a target cluster. Topic names are kept by default. Exact and regex mappings are optional.
- Keys, values, headers, partitions and timestamps are kept. The target broker assigns new offsets.
- Source offsets are committed only after the target acknowledges the write. A restart resumes from the last committed offset. Writes are idempotent by default.
- When a source topic is deleted and created again, the job follows the new Kafka topic ID and copies the new topic from its earliest offsets.
- TLS, mTLS, SASL PLAIN, SCRAM and Kerberos are supported.
- Access is role based: admin, operator, monitoring and compliance.
- Job metrics, lag, an audit trail and scheduled compliance reports are built in.
- Replication halt (tech preview) is off by default and admin-only. It can stop a bad write spreading to the backup.
- The server is one binary with a dashboard. It also runs in Docker, or in Kubernetes with the Helm chart. On kind or k3s, pass a values file with `volumePermissions.enabled: true` when default storage does not honor `fsGroup`.
- `mirror-cli` and `admin-cli` support shell completion for Bash, Zsh, Fish and PowerShell.
- Job commands refuse to run until a job is selected or the id is passed.
- A published image reports `v2.0.0` in the API, the UI and `--version`. A local build reports `dev`.
- Password flags were removed. Tokens, keys and passwords are not printed. The token file is always mode `0600`. CORS ships as `http://localhost:8080` instead of `*`.

What it is not:

- It is not tied to KafScale. KafScale is one supported target, useful when you want a backup on S3 that a bad delete on the source does not reach.
- A replica copies deletes and bad writes. For a backup, use a separate target with separate credentials.
- It does not keep source offsets on the target, and it does not copy consumer groups or ACLs. It does not do point-in-time restore of a topic.
